definition: Bank-conflict overhead is the causal pre-service delay of a memory request during intervals in which the request is eligible for Bank service but the same decoded physical Bank is occupied by one or more memory requests belonging to different inference requests.
included: waiting while the decoded physical Bank is occupied by another inference request
cross-request Bank arbitration or serialization delay
the cross-request waiting portion caused by row switching on the occupied Bank
excluded: the request's own normal DRAM service
NoC, compute, PCIe/DMA, dependency and barrier delay
controller or data-bus delay while the decoded Bank is available
row miss or row conflict without cross-request temporal overlap
Bank access imbalance without temporal overlap
per_request_metric: integral over the eligible-to-grant interval of the indicator that the decoded Bank is occupied by a different inference request
end_to_end_counterfactual: normal makespan minus a paired run that removes only cross-request same-Bank blocking while preserving own service, same-request contention and all non-Bank resources
claim_gate: paired no-cross-request-contention run reduces end-to-end runtime
the effect is stable across pre-registered cohorts or is explicitly labeled exploratory
forbidden_aliases: actual_cycles minus ideal_cycles is pure Bank-conflict time
Bank traffic imbalance alone proves contention
